subject: Private offer: invoicing to distributor & list-price floor clarification
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Thompson <olivia@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:12:00Z
Subject: Private offer: invoicing to distributor & list-price floor clarification

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We can absolutely put together a GCP private offer for the reserved capacity bundle you sketched out. Two quick operational questions that will affect final pricing and the quote we send to your procurement team:

1) Invoicing flow: you mentioned your preferred procurement route is for the distributor (EdgeWave Distribution) to be the billed party on the invoice. Can you confirm whether that needs to be a vendor-issued invoice to the distributor (i.e., Redwood issues invoice to EdgeWave) or you need the marketplace private offer but with revenue pass-through to the distributor?

2) List-price floor / channel margin: our marketplace pricing minimums constrain how low we can list an SKU. If you need distributor margin on top of the private offer discount, we typically model that as either (A) Redwood offers a slightly higher private-offer list price and EdgeWave applies their reseller discount, or (B) Redwood invoices EdgeWave at the net price and EdgeWave invoices NimbusData. Either approach has different bookkeeping and requires different contract language.

To move quickly, can you confirm: a) exact distributor entity name for invoicing, b) whether EdgeWave needs to appear as the billed-to party on Redwood's invoice, and c) an approximate target effective margin for EdgeWave (e.g., 5%–12%). I attached a quick pricing options spreadsheet showing both paths so you can see the implications.

If you prefer, we can include your contracts team on the next thread — copied Kimberly to help with PO flow and channel margin modeling.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Thompson <olivia@nimbusdata.com>

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear options. Short answers below and a couple of follow-ups from procurement:

1) Distributor entity: EdgeWave Distribution LLC (EIN 12-3456789). Procurement prefers Redwood issue the invoice to EdgeWave directly if Redwood is able to do that. They have finance controls that make downstream invoicing messy otherwise.

2) Billed-to party: yes, EdgeWave should be on the invoice.

3) Target margin: EdgeWave is looking for ~6% gross margin post-rebate for this initial pilot. They asked whether that could be reflected as an explicit reseller fee in our private-offer pricing or handled by separate invoicing.

Procurement also asked for a draft reseller addendum and confirmation that the private offer will not prevent Nimbus from listing usage against their corporate GCP billing account (they manage usage attribution).

I'll attach procurement's standard reseller details in a follow-up to contracts@nimbusdata.com — copying them here. Can Kimberly confirm that Redwood can issue invoices to EdgeWave and what documentation we'll need?

Best,
Olivia
Director, Cloud Partnerships | NimbusData

Attachment: (they will send their reseller form to contracts@nimbusdata.com)

Kim / Karthik —

Forwarding Olivia's reply. Quick internal notes and asks:

- EdgeWave as billed party is feasible but we need procurement to sign our reseller addendum and confirm W-9 / tax details.
- If we invoice EdgeWave directly we will treat it as a channel pass-through sale; accounting needs the reseller agreement and explicit margin / commission line to reconcile revenue recognition.
- Pricing impact: to preserve Nimbus effective price and EdgeWave margin, we can either raise the private-offer list price by ~6% (keeps marketplace listing clean) or invoice net to EdgeWave and let them invoice Nimbus. The latter is operationally heavier but keeps list price lower in the marketplace.

Action items:
1) Kimberly: can you confirm accounting's stance on issuing invoice to EdgeWave and what docs they require (reseller addendum, vendor W-9, PO flow)?
2) Karthik: can you run a quick model on the two approaches (list-price uplift vs invoice-to-distributor) showing impact on Redwood gross rev and expected commission accruals? I've attached the pricing options again.

Thanks — short timeline from Nimbus (procurement wants PO in ~10 business days).

Jordan
